issues.legal_issue: An administrative authority cannot use a power of review that the governing law does not confer to set aside an earlier order of a coordinate authority.
material_facts: An earlier administrative order verified a claim and compensation was later quantified on that basis.
A subsequent officer purported to review the earlier verification and rejected the claim in full.
The parties accepted that the subsequent order was made in exercise of review, rather than revision.
The Court found no review power in the governing statute.
issues.conclusion: The purported review order was invalid and could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: The Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954 did not confer the review power exercised to vacate the earlier order. Section 24 of that Act provided a distinct power of revision, but the Court held that the order before it was one of review, not revision. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: administrative_claim_proceeding and earlier_order_by_coordinate_authority and later_officer_purported_to_reverse_earlier_order and later_action_was_review and governing_law_grants_no_review_power

predicates.administrative_claim_proceeding: The matter concerns an administrative determination of a claim.
predicates.earlier_order_by_coordinate_authority: An administrative authority made an earlier order that a later authority treated as an order of a coordinate authority.
predicates.later_officer_purported_to_reverse_earli: A later officer purported to set aside or reverse the earlier order.
predicates.later_action_was_review: The later officer acted by way of review rather than by way of revision.
predicates.governing_law_grants_no_review_power: The governing law does not confer on the authority a power to review the earlier order.

issues.definition: When an officer purports to review and reverse a coordinate authority’s earlier order in an administrative claim proceeding, and the governing law grants no review power, the purported review order is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A person must receive a fair hearing before an authority makes a prejudicial order in a revision proceeding.
material_facts: The Court distinguished the purported review from the separate revision power available under Section 24 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954.
The Court left it open to the Chief Settlement Commissioner to initiate revision proceedings.
The Court directed that no order prejudicial to the affected persons be made in any such proceedings without giving them a fair hearing.
The affected persons were left free to raise all pleas available to them under the law.
issues.conclusion: If revision proceedings are initiated, no prejudicial order may be made without first giving the affected persons a fair hearing.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954 permitted the Chief Settlement Commissioner to exercise revision powers directly or through a delegate. The Court did not determine the full scope of that power, but directed that any prejudicial order in proceedings taken under it must follow a fair hearing and that the affected persons may raise their available legal pleas. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.administrative_revision_proceeding: The matter concerns a proceeding to revise an earlier administrative determination.
predicates.authority_initiates_revision: An authority initiates proceedings to reconsider the earlier determination through revision.
predicates.proposed_order_may_prejudice_affected_pe: The proposed order may adversely affect a person whose interests are involved.

issues.definition: When an authority initiates revision proceedings and a proposed order may adversely affect a person, that person must receive a fair hearing before the prejudicial order is made.
